i0: In English, many nouns have **no article** at all. This is called the **zero article**: *I love **music**. **Dogs** are friendly. She's **at work**.* This page shows when to use ***the*** and when to use **nothing**.
i1: For *a / an* and the basic uses of *the*, see [A, An and The](/blog/grammar/a-an-the/).
tna-general.t: General or specific? Music or the music
tna-general.s: No article for things **in general** (plural and uncountable nouns): *I love music. Cats are clever.* Use **the** for **specific** things: *The music at the party was great.*
tna-general.b0.1.1: ***The dogs** next door bark all night.*
tna-general.b1: With **plural** and **uncountable** nouns, no article means all of them, in general: ***Children** need sleep. **Water** is important.*
tna-general.b2: ***The*** makes it specific: a particular group or thing that we can identify: *the children in my class, the water in this bottle*.
tna-general.b3: Many languages use *the* for general ideas. In English, general = no article: ***Love** is blind. **Nature** is beautiful.*
tna-home-work-school.t: At home, go to work, in bed, by bus, have lunch
tna-home-work-school.s: No article in fixed phrases with **home, work, school, bed, hospital, prison, church, university**, with **meals** (*have breakfast*) and with **by + transport** (*by bus*).
tna-home-work-school.b1: These phrases are about the **purpose** of the place: *go to school* = to study; *in hospital* = as a patient. Use ***the*** when you mean the **building**: *My mother went to **the school** to talk to the teacher.* (She isn't a student.)
tna-home-work-school.b2: With an adjective or a specific meal, use an article: *We had **a** great lunch. **The** dinner at the wedding was amazing.*
tna-home-work-school.b3: American English usually says *in **the** hospital*. Both are correct.
tna-geography.s: No article for most **countries, cities, streets, lakes, single mountains and continents** (*Canada, Lake Ontario, Mount Everest*). Use **the** for **rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, island groups, deserts** and plural names (*the Nile, the Alps, the USA*).
tna-geography.b0.0.1: *the UK, the USA, the Netherlands, the Philippines*
tna-geography.b0.2.1: seas and oceans: *the Caspian Sea, the Pacific*
tna-geography.b0.3.0: streets and squares: *Oxford Street, Times Square*
tna-geography.b1: Use ***the*** with country names that include *Republic, Kingdom, States* or *Union*, or are **plural**: *the Czech Republic, the United Kingdom, the United States, the Netherlands*.
tna-geography.b2: Use ***the*** with *north, south, east, west* as regions: *the north of Iran, the Middle East*. But compass words that are part of a name have no article: *North America, South Korea*.
x.tna-general-s03: Specific group: *the students in my class*.
x.tna-home-work-school-s03: The building: *the school* (or *my school*). She isn't a student.
